name: João Silva
title: Product Designer
summary: Product designer who works close to the code. 4 years on consumer and B2B mobile products, from offline-first field apps to habit loops, with handoff that engineers build from directly (coded prototypes, tokenized design systems). CS background before design.

bullets: Designed a selective offline architecture for monument visits: auto-locked minimum content to avoid silent failures, added a tap to identify fallback in the event of CV detection failure and allowed users to select additional media prior to arrival.

Scaled routes from 10km day walks to 300km multi-day expeditions without splitting the entry point, after evaluating 4 competing approaches. Landed on progressive planning layers (day staging, itineraries, daily recaps, condition reporting) that unlock without disturbing the short-trail flow. Now used by Barcelos Municipality.

Field testing exposed implementation drift: undersized targets, collapsed spacing, overlapping components. Rebuilt the design system on Material 3 as 14 tokenized components with 44px minimum touch targets and every state annotated, plus a coded prototype engineers build from instead of interpreting mockups.

Designed the app’s core loop for club chess players, a weekly cycle of plan, practice, record, reflect and adjust. Every screen moves the player around it, and the reflect step connects their practice to rating history from Lichess.

Chose a weekly cycle over daily streaks after comparing daily, weekly and monthly planning, so a missed session is absorbed into the week. Plans can be built by hand, from one of 5 templates, or with “Suggest a plan”, sized to the player’s time, focus areas and rating.
Worked with the developer through the build, not just at handoff: when testing showed a mis-tap on Stop could lose a session, changed Stop to pause first.
Ran a closed beta with about 10 testers, and their feedback changed the core: committed plans can now be edited during the first 2 sessions before they lock.

Evaluated the main web app (usability research and secondary research), presented redesign solutions to the team, and delivered responsive screens and implementation-ready prototypes under the lead designer.
